canonical_statement: Let $f=\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nz^n$ be a transcendental entire function. What is the greatest possible value of\[\liminf_{r\to \infty} \frac{\max_n\lvert a_nr^n\rvert}{\max_{\lvert z\rvert=r}\lvert f(z)\rvert}?\]

must_determine: Prove a universal upper bound Q(f)≤C* for every transcendental entire f and construct functions with Q(f) arbitrarily close to C*; if an extremizer exists exhibit/prove it, otherwise prove nonattainment.
Every approximating/extremizing function used to approach C* satisfies the exact frozen predicate: it is a transcendental entire function, not a polynomial or a nontranscendental limit object.
close_branch_A.statement: EXTREMAL-CONSTANT CLOSE: determine the exact real supremum C* of the canonical ratio functional and determine attainment.

must_determine: A deliberately weakened base theory or an inconsistent auxiliary bound cannot manufacture independence.

Every extremal or approximating function used in either verdict satisfies the exact frozen transcendental-entire predicate (Transcendental ℂ[X] f together with the required differentiability/entire conditions); polynomial or non-transcendental approximants are inadmissible.
close_branch_B.statement: INDEPENDENCE CLOSE: only a genuine independence theorem for this exact real extremal constant in a fixed standard base theory is an alternative to determination.

definitions:
Formal-semantics guard: for this frozen source record the current Lean target signature is exactly `theorem erdos_513 : answer(sorry) =
    ⨆ f : {f : ℂ → ℂ // Transcendental ℂ[X] f ∧ Differentiable ℂ f},
    (liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop)`. Its binder types, predicate meanings, coercions, filters, and endpoint conventions control any machine-level reformulation; the prose statement may not be used to weaken them.
Quantifier-order guard: preserve every explicit and implicit universal/existential quantifier exactly as stated; no finite checking or selected parameter family may substitute for the stated scope.

Limit guard: every lim/limsup/liminf statement is along the full directed sequence specified by the source (normally the natural variable tending to infinity), not merely along a favorable subsequence. A finite limit is distinct from divergence to infinity and from bounded limsup.

Sequence guard: preserve monotonicity, strictness, indexing origin, recurrence/greedy rule, and whether the sequence is uniquely determined or existentially chosen. Finite-prefix agreement is not eventual/global agreement.

f(z)=Σ_{n≥0}a_n z^n is a transcendental entire function on ℂ, with its Taylor coefficients a_n. For each real r>0, μ_f(r)=max_{n≥0}|a_n|r^n; the maximum exists because the terms tend to 0 for an entire power series. M_f(r)=max_{|z|=r}|f(z)|, which is finite and positive for nonzero transcendental entire f.
Define Q(f)=liminf_{r→+∞, r∈ℝ} μ_f(r)/M_f(r). The limiting variable is the full positive-real atTop filter, not integer radii.

The requested 'greatest possible value' is C*=sup{Q(f): f transcendental entire}. A determination states the exact real supremum and separately proves whether it is attained by some f; nonattainment is permitted and does not change the supremum value.
For the primary functional, r>0. The numerator and denominator are suprema on their exact compact/frozen sets; whenever 'max' is used, attainment is proved for r>0.
Taylor coefficients are fixed at the expansion center 0: a_n=iteratedDeriv n f 0 / n!.

The lower_bound and upper_bound siblings are used only in their exact formal sup-over-family quantifier forms; their docstrings' pointwise 'for all f' readings are distinct and are not imported without proof.

known_traps: QUANTIFIER SLIP: exchanging ∀ and ∃, moving an epsilon/constant after the limiting variable, or replacing “all sufficiently large” by “infinitely many”.
SAMPLED-TO-UNIVERSAL: checking many finite instances and promoting the observation to an unrestricted theorem without a valid finite-reduction theorem.
DOMAIN DRIFT: proving a translated/scaled/relaxed version without an exact map back to the original domain, endpoints, and discrete constraints.
STRENGTH CONFUSION: refuting a stronger folklore conjecture does not refute the canonical claim; proving a weaker statement does not prove it.

FORMAL/PROSE DRIFT: a Lean proof is acceptable only if the exact frozen signature is semantically the same target. `answer(sorry)` or independently filled answer metavariables are not permission to choose an easier proposition/function.
BOUND-AS-ANSWER TRAP: an improved record bound or candidate constant is not a determination unless matching lower/upper (or necessary/sufficient) proofs establish exactness.
LIMIT LOGIC: limsup, liminf, full convergence, unboundedness, and divergence to infinity have different negations; a negative close must negate the exact one appearing in the source.
SUP-VS-POINTWISE: a statement about ⨆_f Q(f) is not a ∀f pointwise bound, and conversely.

A reduction to an equivalent-strength open problem, a tautological rephrasing, or a definition of the requested answer in terms of the original target predicate.
A continuous/real-valued/LP/SDP relaxation without a proved integrality or exact-transfer theorem when the canonical objects are discrete.
A stronger-looking statement in a different normalization/domain that does not formally imply the canonical statement.
Any isolated improved upper or lower bound that does not determine the requested value/order/classification.
A conjectured optimal constant/exponent/class based on computation without matching achievability and impossibility proofs.
Declaring the residual cases “open” instead of resolving them or proving genuine independence.
A one-sided asymptotic estimate when the target asks for an equality, equivalence, limit, or two-sided order.
A bound with a constant depending on the limiting variable or on hidden arithmetic data of that variable.
Replacing liminf by limsup, a full limit by a limsup/liminf statement, or divergence by unboundedness on a sparse subsequence.
The known confinement 1/2<C*≤2/π, or any narrower interval without the exact endpoint, is not a determination.
Proving only that sup≤2/π or that values approach some lower bound does not identify C*.
Determining Q(f) only on finite-order, fixed-growth, dense, generic, or any proper subclass of transcendental entire functions does not determine the global supremum.
